propositions: The complexity lock compares branch baseline against main tip instead of merge base, causing it to report false violations when main lowers a ceiling and open branches carry the pre-lowered baseline
Branches that never touch the baseline file still fail the lock after main reduces a ceiling, because the lock reads the pre-reduction value as a raise relative to main tip
The gate should compare against merge-base(main, HEAD) and read the baseline at that commit so only entries the branch itself changed can violate
Shallow fetch with --depth=1 prevents computing a merge base; the fetch must be deepened or the checkout unshallowed before attempting merge-base computation
When merge base cannot be computed, the lock must fall back to main-tip comparison and log the fallback explicitly, preserving fail-closed posture
